text:
olivia: Quick heads-up — I'm running a sandbox deployment isolation check for sandbox-vpc-nyc. Found a couple suspicious things: some pods seem to have hostNetwork fallback and KMS decrypts aren't showing up in logs. Anyone free?

samir: I can dig in. Is this the cluster with the recent netpol PR?

olivia: Yep. namespace: customer-sim. Pod egress looked allowed broadly. Also noticed no CloudTrail Decrypt events for the inference service during replay.

chris: I merged a permissive egress for app-proxy to allow external health checks. Did we scope DNS/health-check IPs or just 0.0.0.0/0?

samir: It was broad — meant to be temporary. We should replace with explicit IPs and block metadata IP (169.254.169.254).

maria: For KMS, confirm whether we're using customer-managed CMK or cross-account grant. Audit events may be in CloudTrail if KMS is used; node logs won't show Decrypt.

olivia: It's AWS CMK bound to the inference role. During local replay I expected Decrypt calls but nothing in CloudTrail for that timeframe.

chris: Quick checks:
`kubectl get pods -n customer-sim -o yaml | grep hostNetwork` to find hostNetwork:true
`aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time ...`
Also check `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-cmk`.

samir: Policy suggestion: deny hostNetwork by default. Only allow via annotation `infra/allow-hostNetwork=true` on pod or svcaccount and require infra approval PR. Also enforce NetworkPolicy deny-by-default for all egress except an allowlist.

maria: Proposed NetworkPolicy for metadata deny (apply to customer-sim):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-metadata
  namespace: customer-sim
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 169.254.169.254/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
```
Note: this explicitly targets metadata IP; we should also add a default deny policy that only allows specific egress to `vault, nats, model-storage` FQDNs via egress to cluster-egress-proxies.

chris: For audit logging: bump apiserver auditPolicy to `RequestResponse` for these namespaces and ship to central S3 with server-side encryption using the same CMK. Fluentd should tag events with `cluster:sandbox-vpc-nyc`.

olivia: Good. For vuln triage: I found CVE-2025-0456 flagged by our scanner for `containerd` in that image. We should treat as medium-high for onprem racks. Triage steps?

samir: Reproduce with `scancode` and check if running privileged. If exploit path requires hostNetwork or CAP_SYS_ADMIN then our hostNetwork deny reduces risk. Make a quick mitigation: patch nodes with updated containerd and rotate images where possible.

jen-oncall: tagging runbook — if we see suspicious egress from a namespace: 1) label ns `isolation=quarantine`, 2) apply `NetworkPolicy` to block all egress, 3) snapshot pod and node, 4) start forensics and notify infra and legal.

sec-bot: Created incident checklist ticket SEC-1127 and linked runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/network-isolation

olivia: Action items: I'll open INFRA-3421 for netpol tightening and hostNetwork enforcement; assign to @samir and @chris. @maria please run KMS audit and confirm CloudTrail retention/lookup. I'll follow up with a short doc and share in #arch.

samir: On it, will post findings in this thread.

chris: I'll prepare a small PR to replace broad egress with egress-to-proxies and add the hostNetwork annotation gate.

maria: Will query CloudTrail + KMS grants and report back by EOD.

olivia: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
